subject: Export assurance & evidence pack for GDPR data transfers - Solace Health
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@solacehealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: DPF Compliance <dpf@dpf-sol.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Request: evidence for EU->US transfers and DPF mapping

Hi Aditya and team,

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal/Privacy at Solace asked us to pull together a short evidence pack so they can validate the proposed cross-border approach before we proceed to contracting. Specifically they want:

- A concise transfer impact assessment (TIA) summary that maps personal data flows (EU datacenter -> Redwood hosted inference in US) and the technical/organizational mitigations used.
- Clarification on whether Redwood relies on SCCs alone or an approved DPF + supplementary contractual measures.
- Controls evidence: encryption at rest/in transit, KMS region and key rotation policy, logs retained for security events, and an excerpt from SOC 2 Type II relevant to change control and access management.
- Current subprocessor list for any parties involved in cross-border routing.

Can you send a short packet we can attach to our RFP response by EOD Monday? If some items require a separate NDA or redaction, flag that.

Appreciate it,
Elena
Legal Ops — Solace Health

---
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@solacehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 18:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: evidence for EU->US transfers and DPF mapping

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. We put together an evidence pack and a short TIA summary focused on your three bullet points. Attaching a redacted set of artifacts you can share in the RFP:

Attachments included (redacted for external):
- redwood_tia_summary_v2.pdf (3 pages) — flow diagrams, legal basis mapping, residual risk and compensating controls.
- s3_encryption_flow.png — diagram showing KMS integration and envelope encryption for model cache blobs.
- soc2_type2_excerpt.txt — excerpt covering access control and change management controls.
- subprocessor_list_mar2027.csv — current subprocessors (note: some entries masked).

Short answers up-front:
1) Transfer mechanism: Redwood supports SCCs and also offers a DPF-based option for EU customers where required. For the RFP we identified the DPF routing profile we would recommend (DPF+Supplementary Contractual Measures) since your use case includes regulated healthcare data. The TIA PDF explains the residual risk and the supplemental commitments (encryption, contractual audit rights, KMS residency options).
2) KMS and keys: Customer keys can be supported in regional KMS (EU region) for dedicated/private deployments; hosted customers can opt for customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) with optional HSM-backed rotation. Key rotation policy: 90-day rotation for data encryption keys; CMKs rotated according to customer policy (we provide rotation hooks + audit logs).
3) Logging and retention: Security/event logs relevant to access and model inference are retained for 13 months by default; we can extend retention for enterprise contracts. Audit trails show requester identity, model version, token counts (aggregated), and request timestamps; raw prompt text is not logged for hosted customers unless configured under a retention agreement.

If you want, Laura can draft an insertable paragraph for your legal team summarizing the DPF + supplement approach. Let me know if any item needs a non-redacted view (we can do an NDA).

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Head of Trust & Product Security
Redwood Inference

---
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@solacehealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: DPF Compliance <dpf@dpf-sol.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 09:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: evidence for EU->US transfers and DPF mapping

Thanks Aditya — received the pack. A couple of quick clarifications from our privacy team after reviewing the TIA PDF:

- KMS residency: can you confirm whether the hosted inference path can guarantee that CMKs and DEKs for Solace tenant data *never* leave EU region (i.e., keys and plaintext decryption only occur inside EU-backed hardware)? If not, what guarantees do you offer?
- Escrow/Key recovery: do you support a customer-controlled key escrow process for disaster recovery where a third-party escrow provider holds a recovery key?
- Logs/sample evidence: the SOC2 excerpt is useful; can we get a short sample of the actual access log format (sanitized) showing the fields you mentioned (user, timestamp, request-id) — just one day of synthetic/sanitized events is fine.

Also Laura — can you share the exact contract clause language Redwood expects to add as a supplement to SCCs when customers select the DPF option? We want a paragraph we can drop into our DPA draft.

Best,
Elena

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@solacehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 00:31:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: evidence for EU->US transfers and DPF mapping

Hi Elena — following up with the contract paragraph and the clarifications you asked for. See text you can drop into your DPA draft (we can adapt wording if your counsel prefers):

"Data Protection Framework supplement: Redwood Inference will process Personal Data transferred from the EU to jurisdictions outside the EU in accordance with the EU Commission Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) and, where requested by Customer, under a documented Data Protection Framework (DPF) combined with the following supplementary safeguards: (a) customer-controlled encryption keys with regional KMS residency options; (b) contractual audit rights and quarterly compliance reporting; (c) commitment to maintain technical and organizational measures as described in Redwood's TIA summary (redwood_tia_summary_v2.pdf); (d) subprocessors engaged in cross-border processing will be listed and updated with a minimum 30 days' notice; and (e) logs and incident records relevant to transfers will be retained for at least 13 months and made available under reasonable request subject to redaction."
Answers to your clarifications:
- KMS residency for hosted customers: For our multi-tenant hosted API, encryption envelope keys (DEKs) are generated and wrapped by customer-managed CMKs if the customer elects BYOK with an EU-hosted KMS; plaintext decryption for sensitive cache operations occurs inside EU-based ephemeral workers when BYOK is selected. For Dedicated and Private deployments we can guarantee that keys and decryption occur only in customer-selected EU-owned hardware.
- Escrow/recovery: Yes — we support third-party key escrow integration for enterprise contracts. This is implemented as an optional feature with defined HSM-backed recovery procedures and escrow holder governance; details are included in enterprise annex.
- Sample log: attached is a sanitized one-day sample logs_sanitized_20270201.json (note: sanitized sample is in the pack). The fields included are: request_id, timestamp_utc, tenant_id (hashed), operation, model_version, outcome_code, actor (role).

Next steps: if Solace wants an unredacted TIA and full SOC2 bundle we require an NDA + secure transfer channel (we can arrange via DocuSign + secure drive link). I can coordinate with our Legal if you send over your standard NDA.

Will circle back after you confirm whether you want BYOK with EU KMS or the DPF only approach.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference
